editorial:
Imagine living in a quiet village where a grumpy priest tells you not to touch a specific tree, and you do it anyway. That is exactly how the chaos starts here. You will meet Rajan, who thinks he knows better than everyone, and Priest Appu, who seems to have a spooky knack for predicting the future. Once Rajan passes away right after cutting down the sacred Pala tree, things get wild. Appu tells the family that five more people are going to die in the next sixteen days. You get to watch Rajan's son struggle between believing this crazy prophecy and trying to prove it is all a big lie, which leads to some really funny and frantic situations.

The acting is great because the cast makes the panic feel real but silly at the same time. You will love the fast pace and the way the tension builds up, though some of the jokes might feel a bit repetitive toward the middle. It is a perfect pick for a family movie night. If you want the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the lush village greenery, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. It is a lighthearted ride that keeps you guessing until the very end.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that Priest Appu was not actually magic, but he knew the tree was home to a swarm of deadly insects. He used the fear of a curse to make the family change their bad habits. The twist is that the predicted deaths were just a trick to teach them a lesson about nature. Everyone survives, and the family finally learns to respect the environment and each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies with a touch of mystery.
